title: Putin Says Russia-Ukraine War Is 'Coming to an End'
excerpt: The Russian president's remarks, made after Moscow's Victory Day parade, coincide with a Trump-brokered three-day ceasefire and a 1,000-prisoner exchange.
body:
Russian President Vladimir Putin told reporters on Saturday, May 10, that he believes Europe's deadliest conflict since World War II is winding down — a striking declaration that landed hours after he vowed military victory at Moscow's most subdued Victory Day parade in years.

**What Putin Said:**
Speaking at the Kremlin after the May 9 Victory Day ceremonies, Putin told reporters 'I think that the matter is coming to an end' about the Russia-Ukraine war. He also said he would be willing to negotiate new security arrangements for Europe, and that his preferred negotiating partner would be Germany's former Chancellor, Gerhard Schröder. On Saturday, Putin told reporters he could meet with Zelenskyy in another country, but only to endorse a comprehensive accord.

**The Ceasefire Backdrop:**
President Donald Trump said Friday that the leaders of Russia and Ukraine agreed to his request for a three-day ceasefire and an exchange of prisoners, adding that such a halt to hostilities could be the 'beginning of the end' of the long war. The Republican president said the ceasefire includes a suspension of all kinetic activity and the exchange of 1,000 prisoners by each country. Yet skepticism runs deep: Trump's announcement came hours after Secretary of State Marco Rubio struck a much more somber tone, saying U.S. mediation efforts have not led to a 'fruitful outcome' so far and that 'those efforts have stagnated.'

**Why Caution Is Warranted:**
Russian forces have so far been unable to take the whole of the Donbas region of eastern Ukraine, and Russian advances have slowed this year, though Moscow controls just under one-fifth of Ukrainian territory. Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky has stated there is no evidence that Moscow is genuinely willing to end the war. Putin's earlier 32-hour Orthodox Easter truce was violated thousands of times, leaving observers with little confidence in Russia's ceasefire proposals.

**What to Watch Next:**
All eyes now turn to whether this three-day pause extends into substantive negotiations — or collapses, as previous truces have, under the weight of continued battlefield strikes.
